title: Why–because analysis
description: Method for accident analysis to determine causal relationships
extract: Why–because analysis (WBA) is a method for accident analysis using graph theory. It is independent of application domain and has been used to analyse, among others, aviation-, railway-, marine-, and computer-related accidents and incidents. It is mainly used as an after-the-fact analysis method, and it is applied to ensure that results are objective, falsifiable and reproducible. The result of such an analysis is a why–because graph (WBG), a type of causal notation used to represent interdependencies within a system and depict causal relations between factors of an accident. It is a directed acyclic graph, the nodes of which are factors. Directed edges denote cause–effect relations between the factors.
